ME 504: Pure and applied thermodynamics including its application to advanced engineering problems; collateral reading and discussion of the classical works on the subject.
ME 505: This course aims to provide an overview of atomistic-scale methods - in particular, ab-initio based methods like Density Functional Theory and empirical force field methods - to an engineering audience.
ME 507: Covers fundamental design/analysis theory and modern developments in gas turbine engines used for aircraft propulsion and power generation.
ME 512: One- and two-dimensional conduction heat transfer for steady state and transient systems with varying boundary conditions.
ME 513: Laminar and turbulent flow heat transfer in natural and forced convection systems.
ME 514: Thermal radiation fundamentals; specular and diffuse systems; differential and integral methods; numerical techniques; industrial applications.
ME 515: Heat transfer processes involving evaporation, boiling, and condensation.
ME 520: Two-dimensional subsonic flow; similarity rules; theory of characteristics; supersonic and hypersonic flows; nonsteady flow; oblique shock waves.
ME 521: First semester of core sequence in fluid mechanics; Navier-Stokes equations, potential flow, low Re flow, laminar boundary layers.
ME 522: Second semester of core sequence in fluid mechanics; continuation of boundary layers, stability, transition, turbulence, turbulent boundary layers, turbulence models.
ME 523: Application of finite difference methods to the study of potential and viscous flows and conduction and convection heat transfer.
ME 524: First of two courses: Scalings, decompositions, turbulence equations; scale representations, Direct and Large-Eddy Simulation modeling; pseudo-spectral methods; 3 computer projects.
ME 525: Second in two courses: Scalings, decomposition, turbulence equations; Reynolds Averaged Navier Stokes (RANS) modeling; phenomenological models; 3 computer projects.
ME 530: Theoretical formulations and methods of solution of engineering problems and physical/chemical processes in various propulsion systems.
ME 532: Fundamentals of chemically reacting turbulent flows in homogeneous systems including turbulent flames, spray combustion, ignition, reacting boundary layers.
ME 535: An introduction to kinetic theory, statistical mechanics, quantum mechanics, atomic and molecular structure, chemical thermodynamics, and chemical kinetics of gases.
ME 537: A study of laser-based techniques for measuring gas temperature and concentration in chemically reacting flows.
ME 544: This course covers ordinary and partial differential equations, linear algebra, numerical methods, special functions, vector calculus, Fourier methods, and complex analysis.
ME 545: This class will facilitate the hands-on investigation of mechatronic systems using a problem-based approach, with specific focus on system-level implementations.
ME 546: Product families, product platforms, mass customization, product variety, modularity, commonality, robust design, product architectures.
ME 547: Statistics, optimization, and robust design methodologies to design products and environments that are robust to variability in users.
ME 550: Analytical methods are developed using the vector space approach for solving control and estimation problems; examples from different engineering applications.
ME 551: High-power energy storage technologies including advanced batteries, ultracapacitors, and flywheels.
ME 552: This course provides an overview of the fundamental principles and methods of optimal control, dynamic programming, and extremum-seeking control, with a focus on the application of these tools to a variety of problems in the energy generation, storage, and management domain.
ME 554: Analysis and design of control systems with digital controllers, including PID, finite settling time, state feedback, and minimum variance algorithms.
ME 555: Advanced problems and techniques in the design of automatic control systems with emphasis on stability, controller design, and optimum performance.
ME 556: Analysis of robotic systems; end effectors, vision systems, sensors, stability and control, off-line programming, simulation of robotic systems.
ME 558: Fundamentals of Robust Control Theory with emphasis on stability, performance analysis, and design.
ME 559: Design of nonlinear automatic control systems; phase-plane methods; describing functions; optimum switched systems; Liapunov stability; special topics in stability.
ME 560: Introduction to continuum mechanics, variational methods, and finite element formulations; application to bars, beams, cylinders, disks, and plates.
ME 561: Shape and size optimization of elastic structures, continuous and discrete solution methods and numerical algorithms, design of compliant mechanisms.
ME 563: Advanced theory of semidiscrete formulations for continua and structures; emphasizes dynamic and nonlinear problems.
ME 564: An introduction to the concept and analysis methods of structural stability; structures under static/dynamic loading and high speed conditions.
ME 565: Application of numerical optimization techniques to design mechanical and structural systems; design sensitivity analysis.
ME 566: This course will provide in-depth and hands-on laboratory experience in metal-based additive manufacturing.
ME 571: Modeling approaches and analysis methods of structural dynamics and vibration.
ME 577: The course develops the theory of stochastic processes and linear and nonlinear stochastic differential equations for applications to science and engineering.
ME 578: Theory and physical interpretation of continuous and discrete wavelet transforms for applications in different engineering disciplines.
ME 581: This course addresses kinematic and dynamic analyses of planar and spatial constrained multibody systems.
ME 590: Continuing seminars that consist of a series of individual lectures by faculty, students, or outside speakers.
ME 596: Creative projects, including nonthesis research, which are supervised on an individual basis and which fall outside the scope of formal courses.
ME 597: Formal courses given on a topical or special interest subject which may be offered infrequently.
ME 602: For graduate students helping to teach the beginning thermodynamics course, M.E.
